core: Language processing, cognition, brain and development
Language use, rhetoric, meaning, persuasion and communication across textual and media forms
Text data, large-language-model methods and human-centred reflection on language technologies
Experimental statistics, evidence synthesis and critical analysis of language, mind and communication

trace: Ethical theory, fairness/privacy/responsibility and psychological analysis of human–AI interactions directly support the human-centred AI component. This is not training in linguistic annotation or multimodal language modelling.

Propositional/predicate logic, quantifiers, sets, relations and proof supply a concrete complementary formal vocabulary for analysing structure/meaning. They do not implement natural-language syntax, morphology or phonological theory.
Actual R text-data handling, cleaning, joining, exploration and visualisation provide direct methods for language-data inquiry. No particular corpus or linguistic dataset is guaranteed.

Regression/classification, validation and feature/predictor evaluation provide concrete tools for later language-data models. General prediction projects are not themselves a full computational-linguistics curriculum.

Actual text classification/generation, transformers and Python neural-network implementation give substantial language-technology methods. Image/text project choice does not guarantee every student a language project.

Python structured programming, collections, recursion, testing and debugging are concrete prerequisites for research computing and later text/neural models; no linguistic application is assumed in the gateway itself.
Actual calculus, optimisation and dynamic modelling support quantitative learning/model analysis. Current detailed evidence is not a stand-alone linear-algebra or linguistic-modelling course.

Actual interviews/observations, transcription, qualitative coding/thematic interpretation and reflexive empirical research support systematic analysis of communication evidence. This is not formal linguistic morphology/phonology.

Comparative brain anatomy, microscopy/cell staining introductions and neurobiological mechanisms provide a bounded neuroscience foundation for language–brain questions. The animal/welfare/regulatory focus is not specialist language neuroimaging.

Available description supports neural sensory processing and goal-directed action using cognitive-neuroscience/neuropsychological approaches. These are complementary perception mechanisms; no undocumented speech-perception experiment is claimed.

Actual attention/memory/control mechanisms, attentional-blink experiment, cognitive experimental design and research proposal complement language-processing inquiry. The detailed project is not a guaranteed language experiment.

Available description directly supports language neurobiology, speech production/comprehension, acquisition/bilingualism, semantics, aphasia and reading/dyslexia, with actual hands-on experimental approaches. This is a substantial direct anchor, not discounted for description-only evidence; specific EEG/ERP/DES or clinical assessment/treatment techniques are not established.

Neural signalling, brain organisation, learning and behavioural/imaging/electrophysiological research appraisal prepare cognitive/neuroscientific investigation. Introductory exposure is not specialist neurolinguistic experiment training.

Social cognition, influence/persuasion and group processes provide specific mechanisms for context-dependent communication; critical empirical appraisal and theory-guided design support inquiry. Final work proposes research, rather than conducting it.

Actual multivariable regression, ANOVA/ANCOVA, categorical/repeated-measures designs, assumptions and R-based interpretation directly support empirical psycholinguistic study design and analysis. Language datasets are not guaranteed.

Actual medical consultation, doctor–patient/shared-decision communication, interview practice and cultural formulation contribute communication and illness-context methods. They do not supply speech-language diagnostic instruments or aphasia treatment.

Systematic review, bias appraisal, effect-size estimation and R meta-analysis supply concrete evidence-synthesis methods for behavioural/language research. Taught group synthesis is not a Groningen graduation research seminar.

Actual cognitive/social developmental theories, case analysis and lifespan interviewing supply context for developmental language questions. It is not dedicated language-acquisition/disorder training.

Actual rhetorical argument, discourse types, stylistic choices, audience appeals and speech analysis/delivery provide concrete language-use inquiry/practice. The applied educational storytelling project concerns climate/community, not experimental linguistics.

Direct morphology/syntax/lexical semantics, discourse/turn-taking, modality, deixis and cognitive stylistics connect language choices to interpreted meaning. Textual analyses are substantial language inquiry, while systematic structural-linguistics sequences remain absent.

Actual age-appropriate speaking, debating and storytelling instruction/coaching with primary-school partners supplies applied communication-pedagogy practice. It is not developmental-language assessment or speech therapy.

Actual framing, verbal/nonverbal communication, argumentation, persuasion psychology and reflective field-research diaries support language-use/context inquiry. Sustainability communication is the actual setting, not a promised clinical-language project.

Actual close reading of narrative, point of view, style, tone and poetic form supports the concept’s textual meaning/communication dimension. Literary interpretation is complementary and does not substitute for formal semantics or syntax.

alternatives.label: Language processing, cognition & communication
alternatives.concept: Study how people understand and produce language. Combine psycholinguistics with cognition, developmental psychology, text analysis and research methods, and explore how computers process text.
alternatives.labelReason: Psycholinguistics anchors the programme, with substantial cognitive science, behavioural methods, linguistic analysis of texts and selected language technology.
progression: Brain & Behavior precedes Psycholinguistics and later cognitive and developmental courses. Statistics precedes evidence synthesis. Programming, Mathematical Methods and introductory data science precede neural networks and text modelling.

candidates.label: Structural and theoretical linguistics
candidates.reason: Formal logic and direct linguistic stylistics receive full consideration. The current palette still lacks a sustained phonology/phonetics, morphosyntax and formal semantic sequence needed to implement this separate structural concept. This is a substantive shortfall, not a title-based rejection.

candidates.label: Clinical linguistics, neurolinguistics and speech-language disorders
candidates.reason: Actual Psycholinguistics includes aphasia/dyslexia, neuroscience of language and hands-on experimental approaches and is fully credited in the strongest provisional response. General cognitive/biomedical substitutions do not establish a further coherent, substantively distinct specialist language-disorder/neuroimaging sequence. The combined Hanze pathway also has its own programme structure; absence of a professional licence is not the rejection criterion.

selection.assessment: One provisional response is anchored in direct psycholinguistics, linguistic stylistics and real text/neural methods, with cognitive, communication and research complements. Both additional candidate families were tested against actual course content, including description-only Psycholinguistics. Neither yields a further distinct substantive structural/clinical language sequence. Comparator progression remains unresolved; this is not final comparison approval or a target-level no-match.

blocks: Both address language processing and experimental psycholinguistics. Groningen devotes a separate course to a psycholinguistics project.
Both examine applications of AI alongside ethics and effects on people and society. Groningen also studies language, multimodality and AI literacy.
Both support empirical research using statistical analysis. UCR applies multivariable models and experimental methods to behavioural research.
Structural, clinical and specialist linguistics gaps

notes.text: UCR brings together psycholinguistics, cognition, behavioural research and text analysis. Groningen also has a sequence in phonology, syntax, semantics and language change, as well as clinical assessment, neuroimaging and specialist graduation seminars.

audience.programmeDescription: Groningen’s Dutch-taught Linguistics bachelor studies how people learn and use language, how languages are structured, and what happens when language is affected by a disorder.
audience.comparisonExplanation: UCR offers related study in psycholinguistics and cognitive science. Groningen provides a dedicated sequence in language structure, clinical linguistics and research on language and the brain.
